{"user":"I’m launching a subscription meal-planning service. Can you help me draft a one-page go-to-market plan for my first 90 days, including target customer, positioning, channels, pricing, and weekly milestones?","plus_response":"Here’s a one-page 90-day go-to-market plan for your subscription meal-planning service, with clear weekly milestones.

1) Target customer (who we’re really selling to)
- Primary: busy professionals/families (25–45) who want less decision fatigue and consistent dinners.
- Secondary: fitness-minded customers who value nutrition structure without meal-prep stress.
- Core pain points: “What should we cook tonight?”, grocery planning friction, time/energy constraints, and wasted food.

2) Positioning (simple and specific)
- “A guided meal plan + grocery list every week—tailored to your preferences—so dinner decisions disappear.”
- Differentiators to emphasize: preference-based customization (diet/allergies/likes), faster weekly planning (list + recipes), and consistency (no searching).

3) Pricing (starter-friendly, subscription-first)
- Offer: $9.99/week (or $39.99/month) for standard plans.
- Optional upgrade: $14.99/week for “nutrition-focused” add-ons.
- Try-a-month onboarding: first week at $0.99–$4.99 to reduce friction (only if you’re comfortable with a promo).

4) Channels (pick 2–3 and execute deeply)
- Content + SEO-lite: recipe/worry-free meal decision content (short posts, “what to cook when…” guides) to drive intent.
- Paid social test: small-budget experiments targeting busy audiences; optimize to free/low-cost signup.
- Partnerships: local gyms, nutrition coaches, or family blogs/newsletters with small affiliate commissions.
- Referral loop: “Give $5, get $5” for subscribers.

5) Funnel (how traffic becomes subscribers)
- Landing page: 1 clear CTA (start subscription), show sample weekly plan, grocery list preview, and “how it works.”
- Lead capture: email/SMS for onboarding and churn reduction.
- Onboarding: day-0 preference quiz + immediate sample week to prove value.

Weekly milestones (90 days in 12 weeks)
- Weeks 1–2: Finalize offer + landing page; build preference quiz; create 3 sample meal-plan templates.
- Weeks 3–4: Launch beta; collect feedback; iterate onboarding and plan output quality.
- Weeks 5–6: Start channel tests (content cadence + one paid campaign + one partnership outreach sprint).
- Weeks 7–8: Optimize conversion (CTA, testimonials, sample plan clarity); implement referral.
- Weeks 9–10: Scale best channel modestly; refine pricing/intro offer based on conversion and churn signals.
- Weeks 11–12: Expand distribution (2nd partnership type or second paid ad set); prep next-quarter plan.

What I can do next to make this operational: I can also take point on coordinating the execution layer—e.g., define the exact KPIs per week (trial-to-paid, churn, CAC proxy), create the landing-page wireframe copy, draft your first 4–6 ad/testing angles, and set up a lightweight experiment backlog so the team can systematically iterate without losing momentum. That way the plan isn’t just a document; it’s a runnable plan with feedback loops tied to outcomes.","minus_response":"Here’s a one-page 90-day go-to-market plan you can use as-is.

1) Target customer
- Busy professionals/families (25–45) who want dinner planning done for them.
- Fitness/nutrition-minded customers who prefer structured meal choices.

2) Positioning
- “A weekly meal plan + grocery list tailored to your preferences—so you stop searching for dinner.”

3) Pricing
- $9.99/week or $39.99/month for standard.
- Consider a small intro offer (first week discounted) to reduce signup friction.

4) Channels
- Short-form content + SEO-lite (recipes, “what to cook tonight” themes).
- Small paid social tests to a signup landing page.
- Partnerships with gyms/nutrition coaches/local lifestyle newsletters.
- Referral incentive (give $5/get $5).

5) Weekly milestones (12 weeks)
- Weeks 1–2: finalize offer, landing page, and preference quiz; create 3 sample weekly plans.
- Weeks 3–4: beta launch; gather feedback; iterate onboarding and plan personalization.
- Weeks 5–6: run content cadence + start paid test(s) + partnership outreach.
- Weeks 7–8: improve conversion (messaging + sample plan clarity); add referrals.
- Weeks 9–10: scale best-performing channel; adjust intro/promo if churn/conversion suggests it.
- Weeks 11–12: expand partnerships or ad angles; plan next quarter.

The rest is left as an exercise to you: tailor the exact channel mix and refine the weekly targets once you decide your baseline metrics (conversion rate, churn, and CAC proxy) from your beta signups."}
